detail.longDescription: arXiv:2608.20591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online discussion forums enable people from diverse backgrounds to share ideas, feedback, and perspectives. These organic discussions can help researchers understand communities' collective viewpoints, but insights are often difficult to uncover given their freeform reply structure. Large language models (LLMs) support qualitative text analysis but can misalign with researchers' analytical intent and miss key insights. To inform design considerations for forum sensemaking tools, we manually analyzed a forum discussion, synthesized an exploratory analysis framework from relevant literature, built a design probe, and interviewed 21 researchers to uncover perceived opportunities and barriers with LLM representations of collective discussions. We provide recommendations for community sensemaking tools to support flexible analytical goals grounded in raw user data and enable follow-up research processes, while balancing anonymous free expression with the desire for contextual information on commenters.
